log.text: Measured the stores: 1,752 session-store task logs + 524 module tasks (82 module list files). Task.replay vs SessionIndex.reduce disagree on 71: 38 module tasks completed by a {complete:{}} verb with no `at` (SessionIndex misses them), 33 session tasks with assign.landed_at but empty outcome (Task.replay says running). Worse: Task.replay reads `at` but the item tool stamps `ts`, so 37 module tasks get completed_at = the wall clock (all 'landed today'). Worktree qf-6.

log.msg: Design written: Server/doc/state.md (worktree qf-6); posted on the card. Building class State.

Built Server/State.mjs + test (passes: 6 planted tasks, every bucket, local day, check.ok true; broken copy false 1 vs 2). Real repo: full build 5.7 s, tick 4.6 ms. TaskState is now a wrapper (its test passes); SessionIndex landed 1325 -> 1301 (Task.js rules: 24 landed_at-without-outcome or refused finishes), landed_day today 56 (UTC days) -> 34 (local); PastWork landed 1300 -> 1301; TaskHomes.sync homes 80 -> 82, 0 missing; Asked unchanged.

decision.what: One class, State (Server/State.mjs), in node, folds every task in both stores through Task.replay; state.json is the only place a count comes from. TaskState is a wrapper, SessionIndex takes landed/landed_at from State.fold, TaskHomes.sync takes homes from State.homes().
rejected: keep the three readers and reconcile them (three rule sets drift; they disagreed on 71 tasks, and a reconciler is a fourth)
the structure in the browser only (a model, a script, the handover cannot read it; each tab would walk 2,276 files)
SessionIndex.reduce as the rule set (no state machine: cannot tell stopped, waiting, idle)

decision.what: Task.js rule edits proposed, not made (outside the fence; sent to core/Task's inbox): (1) replay_line: rp.at = line.at ?? line.ts ?? a?.at ?? ... (item tool writes ts; completed_at fell back to the wall clock for 37 module tasks; State fills at from ts on input until then); (2) replay_legacy: landed_at alone is complete (33 tasks); (3) complete(): during replay (this._rp set) do not refuse a recorded complete/finish for an open subtask (sheet-handoff-proof, the one real-check disagreement on 10-17).

TasksPage.js: besides the red check line, one more line so a module task's landed row opens its own page (r.url) instead of a /framework/ai/tasks/<id>/ route that only resolves session ids. Alternative: leave the href, and 18 of today's 43 rows would open a dead page. Also .gitignore gains state.json (machine state, like state.jsonl).

log.msg: Merged worktree/qf-6 into michael/dev (merge.mjs, --no-review: self-review, files in context). Started a fresh `node Server/TaskState.mjs --watch` (detached, pid 33036): it took the state.jsonl lock, so Servex's older child stopped by itself; no restart of Servex or the dev server. Its first line: landed today 43, check walk 44, check.ok false (the one known case). Worktree qf-6 not returned: it holds 2 health-monitor log lines Servex wrote during check_page (ai/board.jsonl, ai/tasks/task.jsonl), not this task's; nothing discarded.

finish.outcome: One state of everything: class State (Server/State.mjs) folds all 2,276 task logs in both stores through Task.js and writes ai/state.json; every task sits in exactly one bucket (2,065 = 1,310 landed + 1 in flight + 275 idle + 37 stopped + 442 stale; 211 moved copies counted once). Landed today: 43 by the task rules, 44 by a separate plain walk; the week 10-11..10-16 agrees both ways (0, 71, 66, 18, 19, 52). The one difference is sheet-handoff-proof, whose finish Task.js refuses because it filed a module task; the dashboard shows it in red, and the Task.js edit is in core/Task's inbox. Design: Server/doc/state.md.

assign.title: State: one structure for every task, with a self-check
assign.outcome: **Every task in both stores now has one bucket, in one file.** class State (Server/State.mjs) folds 2,276 task logs through Task.js into ai/state.json: 2,065 tasks = 1,310 landed + 1 in flight + 275 idle + 37 stopped + 442 stale. Landed today 43 by the rules vs 44 by a separate walk (the old dashboard said 26); the six days before agree exactly. The one difference, sheet-handoff-proof, shows in red on the tasks dashboard until the Task.js edit in core/Task's inbox lands.
